items.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
items.summary: CERT-EU warns of two critical PHP vulnerabilities enabling unauthenticated remote code execution, fixed in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. PoCs are circulating publicly, raising exploitation risk.

items.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
items.summary: GitLab patched a critical flaw allowing unauthenticated arbitrary code execution on GitLab servers; CERT-EU advises prioritising internet-facing instances and compromise assessment.

items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: A critical flaw in the AMP feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write files and run commands as root; Cisco PSIRT confirms active exploitation.

items.title: New Android SMS of Death exploit can remotely crash unpatched phones
items.summary: A public PoC for Android flaw CVE-2026-58882 ("SMS of Death") lets attackers crash unpatched phones or disrupt cellular service via a crafted text message.

items.title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer
items.summary: Cisco Talos details the self-deleting VOLTA infostealer, which exfiltrates credentials, sessions and crypto wallets and uses LLMs to profile victims and rank their most valuable assets.

items.title: Attackers Chain Three Ivanti Connect Secure Flaws to Gain Unauthenticated Root Access
items.summary: CISA added two actively exploited Ivanti Connect Secure flaws to the KEV catalog, including CVE-2026-111357; attackers chain three bugs for unauthenticated root access.

items.title: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3bn crypto heist from Binance
items.summary: The FBI attributes a record $6.3bn crypto theft from Binance to North Korea; Binance says it has covered 90% of losses.

items.title: FBI says North Korea behind $6 billion Binance crypto theft
items.summary: The FBI links the $6bn Binance theft to the North Korean TraderTraitor cluster, the same actors behind the $1.5bn Bybit hack.

items.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
items.summary: Parameter Labs detailed an attack chain against ChatGPT's sandboxed HTML preview/artifacts feature, abusing a MathLive library behaviour to break isolation and reach OpenAI APIs and private data.

items.title: Northflank security breach leads to abuse of customers' AI API keys
items.summary: Cloud hosting platform Northflank told customers to rotate all stored credentials and secrets after a breach led to unauthorized use of their AI API keys.

items.title: Chainalysis discloses data breach from "offensive agentic techniques"
items.summary: Chainalysis disclosed a breach in which attackers used "offensive agentic techniques" to reach internal systems, exposing customer names, emails, user IDs and roles.

items.title: Chainalysis Confirms Intrusion Into Internal Tools and Exposure of Customer Identity Data
items.summary: Chainalysis confirmed an external actor accessed internal tools and non-sensitive customer identity data, but says investigation content, credentials and session tokens were not compromised.

items.title: Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to ‘Autodox’ Victims
items.summary: WIRED reports on the "Volta-Autodoxer" infostealer, which uses AI tooling to aggregate victim data including credentials, card numbers and session artefacts.

items.title: A Shared ChatGPT Link Could Run Attacker Code in Your Session and Read Private Chats
items.summary: Researchers at Parameter showed a malicious ChatGPT share link could execute attacker code in a victim's logged-in session and read private chats; OpenAI rated it P1 and fixed it within eight days.

items.title: Inside a malicious Claude Code-branded extension and its persistent SSH backdoor
items.summary: Microsoft analysed a malicious extension branded as Claude Code that installs a persistent SSH backdoor, and published detection and remediation guidance.

items.title: Binance to resume withdrawals after recovering bulk of $6 billion in stolen funds
items.summary: Binance plans to resume withdrawals after recovering most of roughly $6 billion in funds stolen in a major exchange hack.

items.title: What we know about latest efforts to end US war on Iran
items.summary: US and Iranian foreign ministers say a diplomatic end to the ongoing US-Iran war remains possible.

items.title: FBI blames North Korea for stolen billions from Binance in biggest hack in history
items.summary: AP reports the FBI blames North Korea for the Binance theft, described as the largest hack in history by value.

items.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
items.summary: Binance says it has covered 90% of losses from the $6.3bn hack the FBI attributes to North Korea.

items.title: FBI links North Korea to theft of $6 billion from Binance
items.summary: Reuters reports the FBI linking North Korea to the theft of $6 billion from Binance.

items.title: Putin’s potential G20 comeback risks normalizing Russian war crimes, says Kallas
items.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kallas warned that a potential Putin return to the G20 risks normalising Russian war crimes, rejecting calls to soften criticism of the Kremlin.

items.title: 5th EMPACT Hackathon leads to the detection of 51 potential victims
items.summary: The fifth EMPACT Hackathon in Amsterdam brought 40 investigators from 20 countries together on digital aspects of human trafficking, identifying 51 potential victims and five suspects.

items.title: Shops looted as German cost of living protests turn violent
items.summary: Cost-of-living protests in Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt turned violent with shops looted, coinciding with mass demonstrations in France.

items.title: Security Sunday: Wie real ist die Kriegsgefahr? – mit General Alexander Sollfrank
items.summary: Politico German-language podcast episode discussing the risk of war with General Alexander Sollfrank.

items.title: France protests enter third week as police fire tear gas
items.summary: French cost-of-living protests entered a third week, with police using tear gas against demonstrators.

items.title: Ukrainian evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reunite with family
items.summary: Ukrainian evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reunited with relatives after months of isolation.

items.title: Taiwan says China harassing shipping with east coast patrol
items.summary: Taiwan says Chinese patrols on its east coast are harassing commercial shipping.

items.title: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
items.summary: BBC analysis comparing the electoral defeat of Serbia's Vucic with the earlier fall of Hungary's Orban.

items.title: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
items.summary: More than 320,000 people protested across France over living costs and public services, with clashes between protesters and police as unrest spread across Europe.

items.title: Secretary Rubio has a tough time getting officials at G20 on the same page
items.summary: US Secretary of State Rubio struggled to align G20 foreign ministers on economic and security priorities at the Atlanta meeting.

items.title: Hundreds of thousands of protesters march across France for third week in a row
items.summary: Hundreds of thousands marched across France for a third consecutive week, part of a wider European wave of cost-of-living protests.

items.title: Polish president pushes into top court, accuses PM Tusk of takeover
items.summary: Poland's president escalated a rule-of-law conflict by pushing into the top court and accusing PM Tusk of a takeover.

items.title: Binance says it has covered $6 billion of $6.3 billion stolen in hack
items.summary: Binance states it has covered $6 billion of the $6.3 billion stolen in the hack.

items.title: Merz ‘surprised’ by Asian pushback to ‘Made in Europe’ plan for car industry
items.summary: Chancellor Merz said the Franco-German 'Made in Europe' car subsidy restriction plan drew considerable concern from East Asian capitals.

items.title: From Beginner to Bug Hunter: Learning Cybersecurity in the AI Era.
items.summary: Sponsored-style piece noting AI-generated vulnerability reports are flooding bug bounty programs, with guidance for new researchers on producing reproducible findings.

items.title: Wireshark 5.0.0rc1 Release, (Sat, Oct 31st)
items.summary: Wireshark 5.0.0rc1 release candidate published ahead of a new major version.

items.title: YARA-X 1.22.1 Release, (Sat, Oct 31st)
items.summary: YARA-X 1.22.1 bugfix release published with two fixes.

items.title: YARA-X 1.22.0 Release, (Sun, Oct 25th)
items.summary: YARA-X 1.22.0 released with 11 improvements and 9 bugfixes.

items.title: Zelenskyy urges US to speed up Patriot deliveries
items.summary: Zelenskyy urged faster US Patriot deliveries after Washington approved the sale of 500 interceptors against Russian ballistic missiles.

items.title: Meta’s Muse Could Upend All Kinds of Businesses. It Hasn’t Yet
items.summary: WIRED analysis of Meta's Muse AI agent and companies' efforts to frame agentic AI as an opportunity rather than a disruption threat.

items.title: Polish president Nawrocki pushes his way into top court amid rule-of-law tussle
items.summary: Polish President Nawrocki physically entered the constitutional court past protesters, escalating the rule-of-law dispute with PM Tusk.

items.title: An AI Agent Injected Drugs Into a Live Mouse’s Brain
items.summary: A biotech startup allowed an AI agent to select and administer a gene therapy injection in a live mouse, illustrating expanding autonomy of agents in physical workflows.

items.title: Special episode: An exclusive interview with Canadian PM Mark Carney
items.summary: Politico interview with Canadian PM Mark Carney on closer EU-Canada partnership and transatlantic relations.
